# Historical URL audit — 13 November 2026

Scope: owner-supplied Google Search Console examples; source and Git-history audit only. Main inspected at `4d972f29417fa60366ebdb6348e1599208f6ae08`; staging baseline `ce312f68b9ace4bd7d5df0334589007ff329a0e8`. No production configuration or files changed by this audit.

The owner's Search Console examples establish that Google encountered missing URLs. They do not establish their current deployed status, the proportion of important missing pages, or a cause of the 152 discovered/not-indexed and 16 crawled/not-indexed URLs. The current production HTTP result must be read from the separate request evidence. Repository absence is not an HTTP response.

- Read root `AGENTS.md`, the current `versions/2026-11-13-01` reference pointer and applicable master/matrix/register/page-map entries, and the owner’s 13 November technical repair instruction. Original named company Sources remain unavailable; no business policy is inferred.

- Both contain the approved `/assets/images/logo-icon.png` asset: PNG, RGBA, **192 × 124**. It is not square; format conversion must preserve the existing logo and aspect ratio, with transparent padding if necessary.
- A committed customer HTML/CSS/JavaScript/XML/TXT `href`/`src` scan on both revisions found **zero links** to the supplied historical paths. Current source searches likewise found no outdated references to repair.
- Available local Git history contains 585 commits. Searches of historical file paths and matching HTML/JSON/JS/CSS changes found no `detail-w24.html`, `detail-w231.html`, root `style.css`/`favicon.ico`, or mappings for the supplied WordPress product/category/upload names. This does not establish that the earlier external WordPress website never contained them.
- Existing exact aliases are generated by `scripts/build_public_routes.py` from approved route data. None proves an equivalent replacement for the URLs below. A broad category resemblance is insufficient evidence for a permanent redirect.

## HTTP and hosting follow-up

There is no root `404.html` in either inspected baseline revision. Cloudflare Pages can use SPA fallback when no top-level 404 document is present; GitHub Pages and explicit Functions routing may behave differently. Before/after Wrangler testing now confirms this behavior locally; the repaired repository returns genuine404 for the unsupported historical paths. This is not a verified production soft-404 finding. Test the full legacy examples plus an intentionally nonexistent random route on apex and www, checking HTTP status and body. If Pages falls back to homepage with 200, an explicit real 404 boundary is appropriate; do not use a catch-all homepage redirect. Preserve security, legitimate application routes and existing exact redirects.

The conventional favicon repair will not establish Google indexing or explain all missing URLs. Removed URLs can legitimately remain 404. Further evidence requires the complete Search Console affected-URL exports, referring pages, last crawl dates and current production responses.

Actual production checks attempted for all exact supplied examples (except incomplete upload filenames) were blocked by the managed proxy (CONNECT403), before an origin response was verified. See TECHNICAL_SEO_AUDIT_2026-11-13.md for the implemented fixes and production limitations.
